name: application-player-card
title: Player Card
description: Gaming profile card with a gradient header showing avatar, gamertag, and rank tier badge, plus a row of quick stats below.
useWhen: A gaming app or leaderboard needs a compact player identity card with rank and quick stats.
You want a visually distinct gradient header to give the card game-like personality, separate from standard app chrome.
The stats shown are a fixed, small set (3 columns fits cleanly) rather than an open-ended list.
avoidWhen: The context is a standard business app, not gaming — use contact-card or a plain profile header instead of the game-styled treatment.
You need more than 3-4 stats — extend the grid or link out to a full profile page rather than cramming more columns in.
Rank isn't tier-based (bronze/silver/diamond, etc.) — swap the badge for a plain numeric rank display.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a fixed max-w-xs block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: The rank tier is shown as visible text with an icon, never conveyed by badge color alone.
Gamertag text truncates with an ellipsis rather than overflowing or wrapping unpredictably in the fixed-width header.
Stat values and labels are always paired as visible text, keeping numbers meaningful without extra context.

variants.title: Player card
variants.description: Gradient header with avatar, gamertag, and a 'Diamond III' rank badge, plus Wins/K:D/Level quick stats.
accessibility: White text on the gradient header maintains sufficient contrast against both ends of the violet-to-blue gradient.

variants.title: Player card (Dark)
variants.description: Player card adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Stat row text and divider colors must meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark card body.
